body: `BookCover` has a proper designed fallback — `.fallbackTitle` (4-line clamp), `.fallbackAuthor` (ellipsised) and `.fallbackMark` (the NEXTGEN wordmark in `--accent-text`) in `BookCover.module.css`. It renders correctly for books with **no cover recorded**: verified live, those cards show a tidy title/author/mark block. It does NOT cover the other missing-cover case. When a cover IS recorded but the image request **fails** (file moved or deleted on disk, proxy error, slow or dropped network), the `` simply breaks and the browser paints its own broken-image glyph plus the raw `alt` string as unstyled text in the corner of an empty box: [broken icon] The Importance of Being Earnest: A Trivial Comedy for Serious People [broken icon] Crime and Punishment [broken icon] Frankenstein; or, the modern prometheus Reproduced by aborting `**/cover/**` with Playwright route interception at 1440px and 390px, dark theme. Both widths, catalog grid and the Discover rail. The designed fallback and the broken-image state appear side by side in the same grid, which is what makes it obvious: the right-hand cards render the intended NEXTGEN fallback while the intercepted ones render browser chrome. So the gap is the `onError` path on the ``, not the fallback itself — the component already knows how to draw this, it just doesn't switch to it when a load fails rather than being absent. Worth checking whether the same applies to the reader and to `MoreByAuthor`, which reuse the cover component. Note the real-world case is the unstyled one: a cover recorded in `metadata.db` whose file is missing is a routine outcome of moving a library, and it is more common than a book with no cover at all. Method + full inventory: `notes/UI-SWEEP-INVENTORY.md` (outer workspace).
title: A cover that fails to load shows browser alt text, not the designed fallback
